task.name: forge triage: deterministic finding-backlog report with verified-staleness evidence
task.story_text:
## What

`forge triage` MVP: a read-only, deterministic report over the finding backlog. No agents, no spend, no mutation — inventory plus mechanically gathered staleness evidence, rendered for the operator and emitted as a structured artifact downstream triage stages can consume.

The backlog is every open issue carrying a recognized finding label (`forge-finding`, `review-finding`, `needs-triage`). For each finding the report gives age, current milestone or pool state, and staleness evidence: whether the artifacts the finding cites still exist, and whether the cited code has churned since the finding was filed.

## Why

Slice 1 of epic #1033. The evidence-quality bar from #717 is that "probably stale" must become **verified stale** — and that is a mechanical check, not a judgment call. It belongs before any agent renders an opinion (deterministic first, LLM fallback — the ADR-0001 pattern). The last full triage (2026-07-09) was done entirely by hand with none of this evidence available.

## Acceptance criteria

- Running the report changes nothing and spends nothing: it performs no tracker writes of any kind and makes no model calls, regardless of what it finds.
- Every open issue in the backlog (as defined above) appears in the report exactly once. A finding whose evidence cannot be gathered (unparseable citation, missing artifact reference, API failure) is reported as **unverified** with the reason — never silently omitted and never marked stale.
- Every staleness claim is mechanical and cited: it names the artifact checked and the observed result (cited path absent, cited symbol no longer present, cited file changed N times since the finding was filed). No probabilistic or model-generated claims appear in this slice's output.
- An empty backlog produces a report saying so and a success exit — not an error, not silence.
- The report is emitted both human-readable and as a structured artifact whose format is documented, so later triage stages consume it without re-deriving the evidence.

## Example

```
forge triage
FINDING BACKLOG — 15 open (14 hygiene-pool, 0 needs-triage, 1 unpooled)

#1312  bug,p2   Hygiene   age 84d   STALE-EVIDENCE: cited symbol
       _validate_auto_api_fallback_schema absent from current tree
#1124  bug,p2   Hygiene   age 102d  ACTIVE: cited file changed 11 times
       since filing; finding text still matches current code
#659   bug,p2   Hygiene   age 197d  UNVERIFIED: body cites no
       checkable artifact (prose-only finding)

structured report: .forge/triage/report-<run>.yaml
```

## Non-goals

- No disposition proposals, no agent involvement — that is the next slice.
- No changes to how findings are filed or labeled at creation (#810 behavior unchanged).

handoff.summary: Implemented `forge triage` as a new thin CLI plus a stdlib-only deterministic report core. The new flow paginates GitHub backlog reads for `forge-finding`, `review-finding`, and `needs-triage`, deduplicates issues across labels, derives milestone/pool placement, parses conservative file and symbol citations, gathers only mechanical filesystem/git evidence (path presence, symbol presence, churn since filing), renders human-readable output, and always writes a documented YAML artifact at `.forge/triage/report-<run_id>.yaml`. Added focused tests for pagination, deduplication, evidence states, empty backlog success, artifact writing, and CLI dispatch.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] The implementation satisfies the deterministic read-only triage report slice, and targeted triage tests pass. | [anthropic-opus-cli] Deterministic triage report is well-structured and read-only, but any slash-containing prose token (URLs, 'and/or', 'file.py:142') is treated as a cited repo path and its absence is reported as verified STALE-EVIDENCE.

findings.description: A finding whose body contains an ordinary URL, a prose slash phrase, or a file:line reference is reported as STALE-EVIDENCE citing a token that was never a repository artifact — for example a body linking to https://github.com/fuzzypete/theforge/issues/1033 yields the row "STALE-EVIDENCE: cited path absent from current tree" with checked artifact "com/fuzzypete/theforge/issues/1033", and bodies containing "and/or", "read/write", "N/A", or "src/theforge/cli/main.py:142" produce the same false stale verdict.

Symbol presence is decided by a plain substring test over whole file contents, so a cited symbol that only appears as a fragment of a longer identifier or inside a comment is reported as still present in the current tree.

Repo-wide symbol searches re-read and decode every tracked file for each unresolved symbol of each finding, so a backlog of many prose-cited symbols scales as findings times symbols times repository size.

The citation-parsing tests only exercise clean backtick-quoted paths and symbols, so no test covers finding bodies containing URLs, prose slashes, or file:line references, which is how the false stale verdicts went unnoticed.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 proposes one gh issue list query per recognized label but never requires pagination or tests a multi-page result. The installed CLI defaults gh issue list to --limit 30, so any label with more than 30 open findings will be truncated and the command will still report success, violating exact backlog membership. The repository already demonstrates the necessary uncapped pattern in src/theforge/sprint/query.py::_gh_api_paginate_issues.
  Suggestion: Require exhaustive pagination for every label query, such as extending the existing gh api --paginate pattern to return body, labels, milestone, and created time; treat failure of any label query as enumeration failure; and add a test whose results span multiple pages.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 1: the plan's pool-state convention (labels ending in -pool, else unpooled) is invented — hygiene-pool appears nowhere in the repo (only in .forge/plan.md and the trace), so there is no existing label taxonomy to confirm it against. No acceptance criterion depends on pool classification, so this does not block, but the report header buckets could be empty/wrong against the real tracker.
  Suggestion: Have the dev confirm actual pool label names via gh label list on this repo before hard-coding, and document the derived convention in docs/reference/triage-report-artifact.md (Step 5) so the header buckets are traceable.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2's symbol check falls back to 'deterministic repository text search' when no cited file is available. A repo-wide grep for a short or common identifier can report a symbol present (or absent) for reasons unrelated to the finding, which weakens the 'names the artifact checked and observed result' guarantee even though the check remains mechanical.
  Suggestion: Restrict the fallback to identifier-shaped tokens above a minimum length and record the search scope in the evidence record (e.g. checked: repo-wide text search for <symbol>), so the observed result is self-describing rather than implying a targeted file check.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 specifies the artifact path .forge/triage/report-<run>.yaml but the plan never defines where <run> comes from, so repeated invocations could collide or overwrite.
  Suggestion: Use a deterministic timestamp-based run id (matching how other .forge report artifacts are named) and assert the naming in the Step 6 artifact test.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 says 'Register triage in main.py' but main.py wires commands in two places: the register_parser call list (~lines 75-100) and the handler dispatch mapping (~line 140, e.g. 'knowledge-report': knowledge_report.cmd_knowledge_report). Touching only one leaves the command unreachable.
  Suggestion: Add the import, the triage.register_parser(subparsers) call, and the dispatch-dict entry; the Step 6 CLI-registration test should exercise dispatch, not just parser presence.

finding_registry.description: A finding whose body contains an ordinary URL, a prose slash phrase, or a file:line reference is reported as STALE-EVIDENCE citing a token that was never a repository artifact — for example a body linking to https://github.com/fuzzypete/theforge/issues/1033 yields the row "STALE-EVIDENCE: cited path absent from current tree" with checked artifact "com/fuzzypete/theforge/issues/1033", and bodies containing "and/or", "read/write", "N/A", or "src/theforge/cli/main.py:142" produce the same false stale verdict.

Symbol presence is decided by a plain substring test over whole file contents, so a cited symbol that only appears as a fragment of a longer identifier or inside a comment is reported as still present in the current tree.

Repo-wide symbol searches re-read and decode every tracked file for each unresolved symbol of each finding, so a backlog of many prose-cited symbols scales as findings times symbols times repository size.

The citation-parsing tests only exercise clean backtick-quoted paths and symbols, so no test covers finding bodies containing URLs, prose slashes, or file:line references, which is how the false stale verdicts went unnoticed.

A finding body that references a host and path without a URL scheme, such as github.com/fuzzypete/theforge/blob/main/README.md or www.example.com/docs/guide.md, is still treated as a cited repository path and reported as STALE-EVIDENCE because that token is absent from the tree.

An extensionless citation whose leading directory is not one of the six hardcoded repository roots, for example lib/handlers/dispatcher, is dropped during parsing and the finding is then reported as UNVERIFIED with the reason that the body cites no checkable artifact, even though the body did cite one.

The evidence backend now retains the decoded text of every file it inspects for the lifetime of the report, so a run that performs a repo-wide symbol search holds the full text of the tracked tree in memory until the command exits.

A finding body that names a module by its dotted-free path without an extension, such as src/theforge/cli/triage, is reported as STALE-EVIDENCE with the observation that the cited path is absent from the current tree, even though src/theforge/cli/triage.py exists and is tracked.

A body that clearly references artifacts but whose references are all rejected as external, for example one citing github.com/fuzzypete/theforge/blob/main/README.md, is reported as UNVERIFIED with the reason that the body cites no checkable artifact and is a prose-only finding.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
